scope: All 26 samples placed in purgatory by the prior VSIX endpoint review.
question: Would an endpoint security engineer side hostile, benign, or unsure?
assumptions: Unexpected endpoint discovery; no approved research exercise or approved enterprise source-monitoring deployment is supplied.
Artifact behavior and a likely incident-triage disposition are assessed; merely finding an archive does not prove that it was installed or executed.
classification_basis: Human endpoint judgments use actual behavior and authorization boundaries. A scanner score, package name, vulnerability, obfuscation, or missing provenance alone is not a maliciousness verdict.
limitations: This is not a claim that all dependencies/native modules were exhaustively reverse-engineered; each unsure case records the missing path.
These are revised endpoint judgments. Existing Hopper labels are preserved in this review report; no automatic relabeling or detection-coverage completion is claimed.

primary_sources.role: Original Count Dooku campaign research corroborating the three locally observed persistent-ID beacons; no exact-hash listing claimed.
OpenSSF malicious-package advisory for the two withdrawn npm wrapper releases.

samples.name: claude-color-theme
samples.reason: The executable matches a documented malicious supply-chain reconnaissance payload rather than merely an unexplained analytics SDK.
decisive_evidence: Module-load IIFE reads or creates ~/.vsx-id, then POSTs its persistent identifier, platform and package identity to beststats.world/ping.
Both commit packages append this independent executable after sourceMappingURL. The theme package uses the same tracking program as its entrypoint.

Primary campaign research documents the same persistent file, collector, metadata schema and appended-program technique. This corroborates the local payload; the report is not claimed to list these exact archive hashes.
remaining_uncertainty: The observed payload is tracking/reconnaissance. Direct source, credential or token theft and a remote-command stage were not found.

previous_review.trigger: Top-level IIFE runs when the entry module loads; independent of invoking a commit command.
previous_review.reason: Unexplained cross-publisher background tracking persists a home-directory identifier and reports to a shared unrelated service. Functional feature code elsewhere does not explain this appended program. Quarantine; the identifier is randomly generated rather than a stolen host profile.
evidence: extension/extension.js: .vsx-id read/create -> JSON(id,platform,publisher,name,version) -> HTTPS POST beststats.world/ping
Commit variants append this code after sourceMappingURL; theme variant entrypoint is the tracking IIFE
Normalized tracking-program SHA256: 23cde90f070d442c3962460f53ae9411d0b22b9aa6e31713c191289fbaa6da08
limits: No remote code execution or transfer of source files/credentials in the tracking program. Provenance and user consent unverified.

correction_or_new_evidence.finding: Campaign corroboration was missing from the earlier telemetry-only assessment.

samples.name: LingruiAICoder
samples.reason: Treat as persistent source-code exfiltration on an endpoint without approved enterprise monitoring: opening repositories installs commit hooks that send source patches to a fixed service.
decisive_evidence: Activation rc -> uo and workspace-added -> pt -> go -> execFile(bash, install-git-hook.sh). Hook installation is outside the loggedIn gate.
Installer unsets existing core.hooksPath and overwrites hooks/post-commit.

Hook defaults ENABLE_TRACKING=true; git diff --unified=0 HEAD^ HEAD -> diff-patch file -> payload.diffPatch -> curl --data-binary payload to fixed AI statistics service. Commit identity, message and changed-file paths accompany source changes.
remaining_uncertainty: An approved enterprise deployment could authorize this collection. No such context is assumed. Patches contain changed source lines; this is not a claim that all workspace files or credentials are uploaded.

previous_review.trigger: Activation and workspace-folder additions install post-commit hooks automatically.
previous_review.reason: The assistant silently changes repository hooks and arranges ongoing commit/source export outside explicit chat requests. This persistent collection needs authorization that the package does not establish. Keep quarantined despite plausible enterprise analytics use.
evidence: extension/dist/extension.js rc -> uo -> pt installs hooks/post-commit with aicoder-hook-version:0.5
Generated hook machinery unsets conflicting core.hooksPath; full commit patches and identity can enter statistics reports with collectDiff default enabled
Cloud service uses aicloud-center.le365.com.cn; provider login/bootstrap does not by itself authorize repo-wide persistent monitoring
limits: No isolated execution; intended enterprise deployment/consent cannot be established from bytes.

samples.correction_or_new_evidence: The hook actually constructs diffPatch unconditionally when tracking is enabled; the previous collectDiff-default wording was imprecise.

samples.name: notification-blocker
samples.reason: Side benign: notification suppression and user-requested setting changes match the advertised feature. The shared repository credential is a vulnerability, not evidence of an active hostile payload.
decisive_evidence: Activation starts notification/DND timers and downloads a settings catalog; it does not automatically apply all downloaded settings.

applyExtensionSettings reads user-configured notificationBlocker.extensionSettings. Remote catalog entries are applied through the explicit disableExtension UI action; restore/enable paths retain original settings.
Network helper is limited to the configured GitHub catalog repository. No credential harvesting, hidden process execution or unrelated collector found.
remaining_uncertainty: The packaged shared GitHub credential and remotely supplied setting keys/values create a real supply-chain risk. Benign describes the observed artifact, not a secure implementation.

previous_review.trigger: Activation clears notifications and loads community settings; user can apply remote database settings.
previous_review.reason: No theft or remote execution established, but remote settings are writable using a packaged shared credential and are applied to global editor configuration. Cannot clear this trust boundary.
evidence: Reviewed extension.js and both lib modules; GitHub API download/PUT target fixed settings repository, shared credential embedded in split literals, database contains arbitrary setting keys/values and apply operations update global settings.
limits: This is a configuration supply-chain risk rather than proof of deliberate hostile intent; no user credential theft found.

samples.correction_or_new_evidence: The earlier quarantine decision conflated a vulnerable remote configuration feature with demonstrated malicious behavior.

samples.name: antigravity-bridge-extension
samples.reason: Side benign for the program: it implements its openly documented editor automation bridge. Its unsafe listener/authentication defaults need containment or repair, but do not establish a concealed backdoor.
decisive_evidence: README explicitly describes startup HTTP/WebSocket control, sending prompts, running chat actions and reading conversations/artifacts; inspected route handlers implement that feature.
POST /action delegates to declared editor actions such as accepting a pending step or terminal command; it is not a hidden command channel added to an unrelated feature.
Reviewed server uses permissive CORS, no authentication middleware and serve() without a bind hostname. Documentation shows loopback URLs, which does not constrain the actual listener.
remaining_uncertainty: Network exposure and deployment approval remain operational questions. This is a serious unsafe-control-surface finding; do not treat the benign verdict as approval to expose it.

previous_review.trigger: activate -> createBridgeServer when enabled (default true).
previous_review.reason: The exposed automation server can approve agent actions and trigger terminal actions without authentication in the reviewed handler chain; listening omits a hostname restriction and CORS is permissive. An endpoint analyst should quarantine pending explicit authorization and exposure verification.
evidence: extension/dist/extension.js: createBridgeConfig enabled defaults true
createBridgeServer: app.use("*",cors()); POST /action dispatches acceptStep/runTerminalCommand; no authentication middleware in reviewed route setup
serve({fetch:app.fetch,port:options.httpPort}) -> Node server.listen(port,undefined); separate WebSocket server constructed with port alone
limits: Declaration as an automation tool establishes purpose, not endpoint authorization. No proof of attacker tasking or exploitation.

samples.correction_or_new_evidence: A deliberately exposed automation API can be vulnerable without being malware; the former decision did not separate those judgments.

samples.name: kombai
samples.reason: Side benign on the reconstructed fingerprint path: device identification feeds the product’s account/credit controls, rather than a separate collector or credential-stealing stage.
decisive_evidence: Prior static RC4/custom-Base64 recovery reconstructed the fingerprint module without running it: persistent random ID, own SecretStorage value, machine/session/editor/process metadata, encrypted return profile; no file-content theft or exec/network sink in that module.
New trace: activate -> initializeFingerprint; lh registers getFootprintV2 as f3; t7 invokes it. Result enters x-client-context in common API headers and clientContext in agent socket messages.

Account/subscription helpers use api.assistant.app.kombai.com; subscription responses include footprintBlocked/blockReason and credit state. This supplies the previously missing concrete account/anti-abuse context.
remaining_uncertainty: Hidden/misleading fingerprint storage names and device identifiers remain privacy concerns. This is a static triage judgment, not exhaustive reverse engineering of every vendor worker or provenance authentication.

previous_review.trigger: activate -> lazy runtime.js -> initializeFingerprint; provider registers getFootprintV2.
previous_review.reason: The main agent is ordinary minified source, but its separately obfuscated fingerprint module hides durable identity under misleading local filenames and gathers editor/process identity for an encrypted footprint. Quarantine pending provenance and collection authorization; no covert shell or credential-theft claim is established.
evidence: extension/extension.js OM: initializes auth/settings, then runtime chunk initializeFingerprint; browser bridge defaults localhost and OAuth callback binds 127.0.0.1
runtime.js: static RC4/custom-Base64 table decoder recovered 435 calls after uniquely matching checksum rotation 26; specimen code was not executed

Decoded module: ~/.config/.node_repl_history_meta/.runtime_state random persistent identity, own SecretStorage editor.workspace.sessionPersistenceId, machine/session/editor/process metadata; getFootprintV2 returns encrypted profile
Decoded fingerprint module has no fetch/exec sink; provider-side use of the footprint needs context. Earlier blanket claim that the entire agent is protected was inaccurate.
limits: Fingerprint may implement anti-abuse or licensing; that purpose and endpoint consent are not established.

samples.correction_or_new_evidence: The missing data-use trace has now been followed into product API headers, agent messages and footprint-based subscription gating.

samples.name: hugofy

No hostname, username, persistent endpoint ID, file read, process launch or remote evaluation in the program.
remaining_uncertainty: The collector relationship and reason for publishing a Hugo-support facade are not established. Metadata telemetry is not, by itself, proof of hostile operation.

previous_review.trigger: Startup activation starts a 60-second timer.
previous_review.reason: Hugo-named package implements only an About command and an unexplained third-party activation report. Quarantine as an untrusted placeholder/tracker, without inflating extension metadata reporting into credential theft.

Complete small entrypoint inspected: no Hugo feature, hostname source, file read, process execution, or remote eval

samples.name: @chatgptclaudeclub/claude-code
samples.reason: npm replaced this namespace with its security holding package. Both sampled releases have historical publication timestamps and are absent from versions. OpenSSF MAL-2025-42192 marks prior releases as malicious.
decisive_evidence: Three wrapper modules are byte-identical across the two archives; their cli.js payloads differ and were separately inspected. Literal Unicode/hex escapes were decoded as data, never executed.

start.js registers hardware/device identity with its own service, obtains provider tokens/proxy settings and starts the CLI with a preloaded interceptor. It can replace ~/.claude.json with a shared account profile.

Active uploadLogEntry filters Anthropic messages responses, extracts usage counters and calls /stats/usage. Generic full-request sendToServer requires serverEndpoint, which the observed initializer does not supply.
Own account login/refresh, remote proxy configuration and plaintext ws:// heartbeat token-in-query are visible. No established export of every prompt, password store or unrelated provider credential.
